Card hover highlight in Lost Cities does not match the actual card size — it is too short vertically (top and bottom) because the tint overlay uses a hardcoded `CARD_H` (130px) instead of the game's `HAND_CARD_H` (137px).

## Problem

Lost Cities uses 100x137 card dimensions (`HAND_CARD_W`/`HAND_CARD_H`), but the shared `HandView` tint overlay system in `src/ui/HandView._setCardTint()` hardcodes `CARD_H` (130) as the overlay height. This means the hover highlight (green tint overlay) is 7px shorter than the actual card.

Additionally, Lost Cities does not pass `cardHeight` in its HandView construction options, so `this.cardHeight` also defaults to `CARD_H` (130).

## Root cause

| Location | What | Expected | Actual |
|----------|------|----------|--------|
| `src/ui/HandView.ts:1896` | Overlay height in `_setCardTint()` | `this.cardHeight` | `CARD_H` (130) |
| `LostCitiesRenderer.ts` HandView options | `cardHeight` option | `HAND_CARD_H` (137) | not passed (defaults to 130) |

Note: `this.cardWidth` is correctly set to `HAND_CARD_W` (100) via the HandView options, which is why the hover highlight width appears correct.

## Fix

1. **`src/ui/HandView.ts` line ~1896**: Change the overlay height from `CARD_H` to `this.cardHeight`
2. **`example-games/lost-cities/scenes/LostCitiesRenderer.ts`**: Add `cardHeight: HAND_CARD_H` to the HandView construction options

## Acceptance Criteria

- Card hover highlight (green tint overlay) matches the card display size exactly — no visible gap at top/bottom
- All Lost Cities card types (numbered, investment, action) show consistent hover highlights
- Other games using HandView (Gym, Main Street, Golf, Sushi Go, etc.) are unaffected — hover highlights continue to work correctly
- Full project test suite passes

## Key Files

- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — `_setCardTint()` overlay creation (~line 1896)
- `src/ui/constants.ts` — `CARD_H` (130) default
- `example-games/lost-cities/scenes/LostCitiesRenderer.ts` — HandView construction (~line 546)
- `example-games/lost-cities/scenes/LostCitiesConstants.ts` — `HAND_CARD_W` (100), `HAND_CARD_H` (137)

## Related work

- CG-0MPNWH6HC006X41U: Create centralized highlight manager for GymHandPileScene (completed)
- CG-0MRGW6RQQ005NJHG: Fix missing card selection and illegal highlights in Gym Hand and Pile Interactions scene (completed)
- CG-0MPDWKITM006Y08I: Port example-games to use shared HandView and PileView components (completed)

# Intake Brief: Beleaguered Castle — cards cannot be selected to move them (CG-0MUHKD7S8007EEAC)

**Priority: High** | **Type: Bug** | **Assignee: Map**

> Fix a reproducible card-selection defect in Beleaguered Castle: the first click immediately after the deal completes is silently dropped because newly registered top cards are not yet hit-testable, and harden selection feedback so a click always produces visible, reliable selection regardless of renderer.

## Problem Statement

Operators report that in Beleaguered Castle they "cannot select any cards to move them". Investigation confirms at least one reproducible selection defect — the first click after the deal animation completes is ignored — plus two aggravating factors (no visible selection highlight under the Canvas renderer, and only the top card of each column being interactive). The result is that a player's click can appear to do nothing, making the game feel unresponsive or unplayable.

## Users

- **Solitaire player:** Wants to click a card and immediately see it selected, then click a destination to move it, without having to click twice or guess whether the click registered.
  - *"As a player, I want my first click on a card after the deal to select it, so the game feels responsive and I can plan moves confidently."*
- **QA / playtester:** Needs deterministic, reproducible interaction behaviour so selection bugs can be captured in browser tests and not recur.
  - *"As a tester, I want a browser regression test that fails if the first post-deal click is dropped, so this class of bug is caught automatically."*
- **Engine developer:** Wants the fix to live in the shared interaction layer (`src/ui/dragDrop.ts` / `HandView`) where the registration race originates, rather than as a game-local workaround.
  - *"As an engine developer, I want newly registered draggables to be hit-testable immediately, so every game using the shared module benefits."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **First post-deal click always selects:** In the natural (non-reduced-motion) boot flow — choose variant → deal completes → immediate first click on a tableau top card — the column is selected on the very first click, 100% of runs (no dropped click, no retry required). Verified by a new browser test that repeats the sequence across multiple boots/seeds.
2. **Selection is visibly indicated in all renderers:** A selected top card shows a persistent, distinct highlight under both WebGL and Canvas renderers (BC currently uses raw `setTint()`, which is a no-op in Phaser 4 Canvas; the shared HandView Canvas-compatible tint-overlay approach must be used or equivalent).
3. **End-to-end click-to-move works from a clean natural boot:** From a fresh natural boot, selecting a top card and then clicking a legal destination (foundation or tableau column) executes exactly one undoable move, with the highlight and selection state clearing/reset appropriately.
4. **Double-click / same-card deselect unaffected:** Clicking an already-selected card deselects it, and clicking a different valid source re-selects, preserving the documented click-to-move contract.
5. **Regression tests:** New browser test(s) under `tests/beleaguered-castle/` cover the first-click and click-to-move flows in the natural boot path; the existing drag/click coexistence tests continue to pass.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, `help-content.json` if the interaction contract changes, and any relevant `docs/` entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Preserve dual-input:** Both drag-and-drop and click-to-move must continue to work simultaneously; the click-vs-drag threshold (`dragDistanceThreshold`) behaviour must be preserved.
- **No behavioural regression for other games:** Any change to the shared drag-drop module (`src/ui/dragDrop.ts`) or `HandView` must not break Main Street, Golf, Coloretto, the Gym, or other consumers. Prefer a fix at the shared layer that is additive and backward-compatible.
- **Reduced-motion and replay/test paths:** The reduced-motion (`__BC_TEST_REDUCED_MOTION__`) and replay paths must remain functional; the fix must not depend on animations having run.
- **Licensing:** All code/assets remain permissively licensed (MIT/Apache/CC0).
- **Scope:** Fix the selection/move reliability bug; do not add a hint-system overhaul or change game rules.

## Existing State

- **Selection logic:** `BeleagueredCastleScene.handleCardClick()` → `selectColumn()` / `deselectColumn()` implement click-to-select. `BeleagueredCastleRenderer.makeDraggable()` attaches the top card's `pointerdown` → `onCardClick`, and registers the top card as a draggable via the shared `DragDropManager.registerDraggable()`.
- **Interaction gate:** `interactionBlocked` returns true while `!dealComplete || gameEnded || autoCompleting`; `dealComplete` is set in the renderer's `onDealComplete`, which then calls `makeDraggable()`.
- **Registration race (confirmed):** Immediately after `makeDraggable()`, the top-card sprites are present in `scene.input` as interactive but sit in the input plugin's pending-insertion queue (`_pendingInsertion`) and are **not** yet in the active hit-test list (`_list`). A click arriving before the next input `preUpdate` is silently ignored. Diagnostic evidence: `sprite.input=true`, `input.enabled=true`, `inList=false`, `inPending=true`; the first click failed in 3 of 5 natural boots, while a retry (or a ≥~500 ms settle delay) always succeeded.
- **Renderer highlight:** `BeleagueredCastleRenderer.selectColumn()` / `deselectColumn()` use raw `setTint()` / `clearTint()`. Per the `HandView` documentation, `setTint()` is a no-op in Phaser 4's Canvas renderer, so no selection highlight is visible when the game falls back to Canvas.
- **Only top cards interactive:** Covered (non-top) tableau cards are not interactive by design; clicking them does nothing. This is intentional but may read as "cannot select" to a new player.
- **Existing tests:** `tests/beleaguered-castle/BeleagueredCastleDrag.browser.test.ts` covers drag-to-foundation/tableau, illegal/out-of-zone snap-back, reduced-motion behaviour, and a click-vs-drag coexistence test (`click without drag still selects a column`). That suite boots in reduced-motion test mode (`__BC_TEST_REDUCED_MOTION__`) and does not exercise the natural deal-then-click timing, which is where the race manifests.
- **Deployment:** The game uses `Phaser.AUTO` (WebGL with Canvas fallback) via `createCardGame`. `origin/main` and `dev` are functionally identical for BC input handling (differences are import-alias refactors and `GAME_INFO` metadata).

## Desired Change

1. **Eliminate the post-deal click race** so the first click after the deal always selects. Investigate the correct fix at the shared layer — e.g. ensure newly registered draggables/interactive top cards are flushed into the input hit-test list (or registered earlier / re-registered on the next tick) before interaction is considered available — rather than masking it with a game-local delay. Keep the fix additive and safe for all `DragDropManager`/`HandView` consumers.
2. **Make selection feedback renderer-agnostic:** replace BC's raw `setTint()` selection highlight with the shared Canvas-compatible mechanism (e.g. HandView's tint-overlay helper) or an equivalent persistent outline that renders in both WebGL and Canvas.
3. **Add natural-flow regression tests:** a browser test that boots without `__BC_TEST_REDUCED_MOTION__`, dismisses the variant popup, waits for the deal, and asserts the immediate first click selects; plus a click-to-move end-to-end assertion. Reuse the existing BC drag-test helpers where possible.
4. **Verify the end-to-end contract** (select → destination click → one undoable move) and document the interaction as tested.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/beleaguered-castle/scenes/BeleagueredCastleRenderer.ts` — `makeDraggable()` registration timing; `selectColumn()`/`deselectColumn()` highlight mechanism.
- `example-games/beleaguered-castle/scenes/BeleagueredCastleScene.ts` — `handleCardClick()`, `selectColumn()`, `wireInput()`, `interactionBlocked`, deal-complete wiring.
- `src/ui/dragDrop.ts` — `registerDraggable()` `setInteractive` / input-list timing; potential shared-layer fix.
- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — Canvas-compatible tint-overlay helper to reuse for BC selection.
- `tests/beleaguered-castle/BeleagueredCastleDrag.browser.test.ts` — extend/add natural-flow first-click + click-to-move regression tests.
- `example-games/beleaguered-castle/help-content.json` — update only if the interaction contract changes.

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks
- **Narrow-window vs persistent symptom:** The confirmed first-click race is short-lived (one input `preUpdate`); on a foregrounded 60 fps browser it is ~16 ms. The operator's "cannot select any cards" may be a broader symptom (perception, device, throttled frames, Canvas fallback). Mitigation: fix the confirmed defect, harden highlight visibility, and add an explicit open question for the operator; treat any additional scenario as a linked follow-up rather than expanding this item indefinitely.
- **Shared-module regression:** Changing `DragDropManager`/`HandView` input timing could affect Main Street, Golf, Coloretto and the Gym. Mitigation: keep the change additive, run the affected games' browser suites, and prefer a fix that does not alter existing drag semantics.
- **Test flakiness:** Timing-based browser tests can flake. Mitigation: assert on deterministic scene state (`selectedCol`, `moveCount`) and repeat the boot sequence across seeds; avoid wall-clock sleeps where possible.
- **Canvas fallback coverage:** Headless CI can force Canvas; verify the highlight fix visually/structurally in both renderer modes.
- **Scope creep:** A broader "make every card clickable" or "rework selection UX" redesign would expand scope. Record such ideas as linked follow-up work items instead.

### Assumptions
- The operator is running the current `dev` code in a standard browser (mouse input); the deployed `main` build is functionally identical for BC input.
- The first-click race is a genuine defect worth fixing regardless of whether it fully explains the operator's report.
- Reduced-motion and replay modes must remain unaffected by the fix.

## Related Work

- **Beleaguered Castle (CG-0MLSDWFLT1WB6IEB)** [completed]: The epic that built the game, including click-to-move, drag-and-drop, undo/redo, and auto-move.
- **Click-to-Move Card Input (CG-0MLTFE68N1TONFIE)** [completed]: Introduced the click-to-move interaction contract this bug affects.
- **Highlight for selected card (CG-0MOJ44AXO006HFAS)** [completed]: Prior critical selection-feedback bug (market cards); establishes the project's expectation of a persistent, visible selection marker and Canvas-safe rendering.
- **Refactor Beleaguered Castle to use the core-engine drag-drop module (CG-0MSKSLDXQ008F5Y3)** [completed]: Moved BC onto the shared `DragDropManager` where the registration timing originates.
- **Add drag-drop browser tests for Beleaguered Castle (CG-0MSN4C4LI007VVGK)** [completed]: The existing BC interaction test suite that will be extended.
- **Reusable core-engine drag-drop module (CG-0MSKT0NQP0018KK6)** [completed]: The shared module whose `registerDraggable()` timing is implicated.
- **Bugs in Beleaguered Castle HandView/PileView migration** (related completed items under the BC epic) — context on recent BC interaction refactors.

### Related work (automated report)

Searched Worklog and repository files for keywords derived from the report (beleaguered, castle, cards, click, deal, first, select, move, ignored, cannot). The automated `find-related` pass returned 3 related items and 3 repository matches:

- **CG-0MLTFCTNK10RQ41T** – Beleaguered Castle Game Logic (completed): the game-logic foundation underlying move legality used by selection/move.
- **CG-0MSRGV53I009BKKR** – Held-event play burst feedback (completed): interaction-feedback precedent in the codebase.
- **CG-0MUF6LBW600657B2** – [test-failure] skills-extensions-tracking.test.ts ignore check is vacuous (open): unrelated test-infrastructure item surfaced by keyword overlap; no dependency.
- Repository file matches: `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` (keyword overlap only — no code paths implicated).

The manual Related Work list above is the authoritative set; the automated matches are broad and mostly keyword-driven.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Does the failure happen on the very first click after the deal, or on every click?** — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (operator). Investigation could only reproduce a *first-click-after-deal* drop; subsequent clicks succeeded. Awaiting operator confirmation of whether their experience is intermittent (first click) or total (all clicks).
- **Q: Are you playing in WebGL or does your browser fall back to Canvas?** — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (operator). Canvas fallback would additionally hide the `setTint` selection highlight, which could read as "not selected". The game defaults to `Phaser.AUTO` (WebGL preferred).
- **Q: Is this the local dev build or the deployed `main` build?** — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (operator). `main` and `dev` are functionally identical for BC input handling, so the same defect is expected in both.
- **Q: Are you clicking the fully visible top card of a column, or a partly covered card?** — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (operator). Only the top card of each column is interactive by design; covered cards intentionally do nothing.

## Suggested Next Step

Confirm the operator's exact scenario via the open questions above, then implement the confirmed fix (input-registration flush + Canvas-safe selection highlight) with natural-flow browser regression tests.
data.title: Beleaguered Castle: cards cannot be selected to move them (first click after deal ignored)
